version.changelog: Refine Playwright install guidance and simplify install metadata

llm.summary: The package is internally consistent with its stated purpose: Node.js + Playwright CLI scripts for Shanghai Library seat booking that read/write local profile auth files and call the library API; nothing requested or installed appears unrelated to that task.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Shanghai Library seat booking) matches the code and runtime requirements. Requested binaries (node, npm, npx) and the documented Playwright dependency are appropriate for browser-assisted login and API calls. No unrelated cloud credentials, system-level config paths, or surprising capabilities are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts limit behavior to: launching Playwright for interactive login, extracting accessToken/sign/timestamp, saving/reading profile JSON files (default under ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking), and calling the library API (yuyue.library.sh.cn). The instructions do not direct the agent to read arbitrary system files or to transmit data to external endpoints other than the library API or Playwright/browser download endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry install spec only ensures Node (brew formula). The runtime instructions require running `npm install playwright` and `npx playwright install chromium`, which will fetch an npm package and download Chromium binaries from Playwright's distribution servers. This is expected for browser automation but is a higher-risk install step than an instruction-only skill because it writes binaries to disk and performs external downloads; verify you trust the Playwright sources and run installs in a controlled environment if concerned.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or external credentials from the registry. It relies on locally stored profile files containing the library's accessToken/sign/timestamp — this is proportional to its purpose. The code does not reference other env vars or unrelated secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no system-wide configuration changes are requested. The skill reads and writes its own profile files under ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking (normal for this use). Autonomous invocation is allowed by default but is not combined with broad credentials or elevated privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to do what it claims. Before installing: 1) Inspect or run the repository locally rather than granting automatic execution—the scripts will read/write auth JSON files under ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking and will save extracted tokens there. 2) When using browser login, you'll be asked to enter your credentials interactively; the script extracts library tokens and will post requests only to the library API (yuyue.library.sh.cn). 3) Installing Playwright downloads npm packages and Chromium binaries—if you prefer, run these steps in a contained environment (VM or container). 4) Keep profile files permission-restricted (chmod 600) and do not commit them to version control. 5) If you do not trust the author, review login.js and scripts/lib/auth.js to confirm there is no unexpected network call or third-party upload, or run the tool behind a network monitor to observe outgoing connections.
